# Ford Taurus Rear Brake Job: How to relieve spring pressure on emergency brake cable

Working on the rear drum brakes of a 2003 Ford Taurus SE is a common task for owners tackling DIY maintenance, but removing the shoes often hits a specific snag: the parking brake cable tension. The parking brake mechanism in this vehicle uses a single cable that runs through the bottom of the brake assembly to actuate the lever on the shoe itself. When you try to rotate the equalizer yoke or remove the springs holding the shoes in place, that cable is under significant tension. Attempting to disconnect the shoe lever from the cable while the spring is loaded can result in the cable snapping back violently, potentially causing injury or damaging the linkage components.

To safely perform this removal, you must mechanically relieve the tension stored in the parking brake system before attempting to manipulate the internal components. The most reliable method involves releasing the tension at the equalizer yoke, which is the central hub where the two rear cables converge. On the 2003 Taurus, this yoke features a specific adjustment mechanism designed for this exact purpose. You will need to locate the small retaining clip or screw on the side of the equalizer assembly that secures the cable adjuster.

Once you have identified the adjustment point, carefully release the tension by rotating the adjuster nut in the direction that loosens the cable pull. This action allows the internal parking brake springs to contract slightly, reducing the force applied to the shoe levers. It is crucial not to fully disconnect the cable at this stage unless you are prepared to support the weight of the slack immediately. Instead, maintain a controlled amount of slack that permits the removal of the spring retainers or the rotation of the yoke without the cable snapping back against the anchor point.

If your specific brake assembly design does not allow for easy adjustment at the yoke while the drum is on the hub, you may need to remove the rear wheels and drums first. Accessing the parking brake lever directly from the outside of the drum can sometimes be difficult due to limited space. In such cases, removing the entire brake assembly from the axle allows for better visibility of the cable routing and spring geometry. This approach trades the inconvenience of disassembly for a safer working environment where you can see exactly how the tension is distributed.

When reconnecting the system after your repair, ensuring the parking brake cable has proper tension is equally critical. A common mistake is to simply bolt everything back together without verifying that the emergency brake functions correctly. After reassembling the shoes and securing the levers, you must check that the parking brake lever moves freely through its full range of motion. If the lever feels stuck or requires excessive force to engage, the spring tension may be too high, or the cable adjustment at the equalizer yoke might still need fine-tuning.

For those looking for broader automotive maintenance resources or needing specific parts diagrams for older models like the 2003 Taurus, checking specialized databases can sometimes provide clearer exploded views of the brake assembly than standard service manuals. While general advice is available online, understanding the mechanical interaction between the equalizer yoke and the shoe springs is non-negotiable for a safe job. If you are uncomfortable manipulating the parking brake linkage without proper tools or guidance, it is often safer to seek assistance from a professional mechanic rather than risking injury from a sudden release of stored spring energy.
